results.title: Effects of Background Checks on Violent Crime
results.content: Using data from 56 large U.S. cities between 1980 and 2010, the author found in his preferred models (population-weighted models with a one-year lag of the dependent variable included in the model, controlling for other state gun policies and including other time-varying state covariates that were interpolated over the period) that pre–Brady Act state background check requirements had an uncertain effect on either firearm homicides or total homicides.
